hook_text: A melktert, 8 slices, and a question: is one eighth bigger than one half? 8 is bigger than 2, right?
clip_script: Bakery in Bloemfontein. One melktert. Cut it into 2 equal slices: each slice is one half. Cut the same tart into 8 equal slices: each slice is one eighth. Which slice do you want? The half! More slices means thinner slices. So one eighth is smaller than one half, even though 8 is bigger than 2. Now the chocolate slab: 8 blocks, you eat 3. That is three eighths eaten, five eighths left, and together eight eighths, the whole slab. Bottom number: how many equal parts. Top number: how many you take. And the parts must be equal, or they are not fractions at all.
visual_style: Whiteboard melktert slicing into halves and then eighths; a chocolate slab with blocks disappearing; a fraction wall building row by row.
pacing: Quick slicing, the surprise about eighths, then the slab and the two-number rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build your own fraction wall from paper strips.
